STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r2.speaker: Many commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r2.claim: Many commentators hold verses 53–55 to be Madinan and say they were revealed concerning Waḥshī, who won freedom by killing Ḥamzah at Uḥud.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r2.anchor: Many commentators maintain that vv. 53–55 are from the Madinan period

STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.speaker: Other commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.claim: A different reported view says verses 53–59 were all revealed concerning Waḥshī.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.anchor: while others say that vv. 53–59 were all revealed in regard to it

STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.claim: The call to repent in verses 54–67 leads into the final extended contrast between the believers’ and disbelievers’ ends in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.anchor: This is followed by an exhortation to turn to God in repentance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.claim: Rather than despairing of God or seeking deities and intercessors, people should turn to the forgiving and merciful God in every circumstance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.anchor: losing hope in God and seeking other deities and intercessors is not the correct way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.claim: People should turn to God and believe in His revealed Book before He seizes them; later regret and a wish to believe will be too late.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.anchor: before He seizes them, people should turn to Him and profess faith in this magnificent Book

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r2.claim: The best revelation to follow is the Qur'an; the phrase does not mean some Qur'anic passages are better than others, since all are good.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r2.anchor: واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم، مثل قوله: الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه، وهو القرآن، وليس المعنى أن بعضا أحسن من بعض، بل كله حسن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r3.claim: The warning means punishment may arrive suddenly while people are unaware, making it more severe for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r3.anchor: من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة، أي فجأة، وأنتم لا تشعرون: أي وأنتم غافلون عن حلوله بكم، فيكون ذلك أشد في عذابكم.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r1.claim: Verse 55 elaborates the previous verse’s call to turn to God: the “best thing” is the Qur’an, called the “best word” in 39:23.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r1.anchor: the best word) in verse twenty three of this sūrah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r2.claim: The Qur’an is God’s final and most complete Book.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r2.anchor: The Qur’ān is the final and most complete Book of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r3.claim: The Qur’an is protected from alteration.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r3.anchor: It is secure from any fragment of alteration.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r4.claim: It calls people to the natural religion and lacks the stern, harsh directives found in previous scriptures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r4.anchor: It invites people to the natural religion and hence is free of the stern and harsh directives of the previous scriptures.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r5.claim: For Arabs, the Qur’an’s lucid, eloquent Arabic is unmatched, and its Arabic revelation is a great divine favor to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r5.anchor: it is in very eloquent and lucid Arabic the very likes of which others are not able to produce

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r6.claim: Its mutashābih and mathānī form doubles its benefit compared with other divine books, as discussed at 39:23.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r6.anchor: This Book was revealed as mutashābih and mathānī as a result of which its benefit doubled

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r7.claim: The Qur’an calls Arabs to Abraham’s religion, a message already familiar to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r7.anchor: This Book invites people to the religion of the great forefather of the Arabs: Abraham

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r8.claim: Given these qualities, people should wholeheartedly welcome and absorb the Qur’an; denying it brings an unimaginable punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r8.anchor: people should whole-heartedly welcome it and absorb it in their minds

IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r2.speaker: عمر
IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r2.claim: Umar says that after the Prophet reached Medina, God revealed these verses about the persecuted apostates and the despair they voiced to themselves and others voiced about them.
IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r2.anchor: فلما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة، أنزل الله تعالى فيهم، وفي قولنا وقولهم لأنفسهم

IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r3.claim: Umar wrote the revealed passage on a sheet by hand and sent it to Hisham ibn al-As.
IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r3.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب: فكتبتها بيدي في صحيفة، وبعثت بها إلى هشام بن العاصي

IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r4.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r4.speaker: هشام بن العاصي
IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r4.claim: Hisham repeatedly read the letter in Dhū Ṭuwā without understanding it; after praying, he understood it concerned his group and their self-talk, then returned to join the Prophet in Medina.
IBNHISHAM:v1p475/r4.anchor: قال هشام بن العاصي: فلما أتتني جعلت أقرؤها بذي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r1.claim: The apparent addressees are the servants addressed earlier, whether that meant believers alone or believers together with unbelievers; what was sent down is the Quran, sent through Muhammad for all people.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنه خطاب للعباد المخاطبين فيما تقدم سواء أريد بهم المؤمنون أو ما يعمهم والكافرين والمراد بما أنزل القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r2.claim: Possible senses of the best are Quranic guidance to the good of both abodes, excluding stories and similar material; obligations; decisive obligations; or abrogating rulings. The comparative form is literal on the first and third readings, while the second and fourth allow two analyses.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بأحسنه ما تضمن الإرشاد إلى خير الدارين دون القصص ونحوها أو المأمورية أو العزائم أو الناسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r3.claim: Another proposed sense is the safest and most secure course, such as turning back to God and persisting in obedience; the comparative then retains its ordinary force.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r3.anchor: لعل الأحسن ما هو أنجي وأسلم كالإنابة والمواظبة على الطاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r4.claim: A less apparent proposal makes the address one to jinn, takes what was sent down as the heavenly books, and identifies the best as the Quran; Al-Alusi notes the departure from the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الخطاب للجني والمراد بما أنزل الكتب السماوية وبأحسنه القرآن وفيه ارتكاب خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r5.claim: Mentioning the Lord encourages obedience to what He sent down.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r5.anchor: وفي ذكر الرب ترغيب في الاتباع

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r6.claim: The warning is to follow before punishment arrives suddenly, with no awareness of its coming and no chance to take measures to avert it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#2/r6.anchor: لا تعلمون أصلا بمجيئه فتتداركون ما يدفعه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r4.claim: The best revealed thing is the Quran, and the Quran is wholly good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r4.anchor: يعني: القرآن، والقرآن كله حسن، ومعنى الآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says to commit to obedience and avoid disobedience: the Quran names bad things to shun, lesser things not to desire, and the best to choose.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r5.anchor: ما قاله الحسن: التزموا طاعته واجتنبوا معصيته، فإن القرآن ذكر القبيح لتجتنبه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r6.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r6.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the best revealed thing as what God commanded in the Book.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p128#3/r6.anchor: قال السدي: "الأحسن" ما أمر الله به في الكتاب،

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r2.claim: The best revelation means Qur’an, commanded rather than prohibited matters, decisive rulings rather than concessions, abrogating rather than abrogated material, or the safest and most salvific course.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r2.anchor: القرآن أو المأمور به دون المنهي عنه، والعزائم دون الرخص

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r3.claim: Act before punishment comes suddenly without noticing its approach, while time remains to recover.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r9.claim: Following what was revealed is a further struggle against the self: follow this Qur'an, the best of God's revealed books, and the best teachings within it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r9.anchor: ولما أمر بروية الأمور كلها من الله وإسلام القياد كله إليه , أمر بما هو أعلى من ذلك , وهو المجاهدة بقتل النفس

BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r10.claim: Among the best teachings are to reconnect with one who cuts ties, give to one who withholds, and do good to one who wrongs you.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r10.anchor: فتصل من قطعك وتعطي من حرمك وتحسن إلى من ظلمك

BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r11.claim: In worship, the highest practice is to act as though seeing God, above merely remembering that He sees you.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p462/r11.anchor: هذا في حق الخلائق ومثله في عبادة الخالق بأن تكون ( كأنك تراه ) الذي هو أعلى من استحضار

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r1.claim: Repeating “from your Lord” names the Benefactor explicitly to encourage people who continue to commit grave wrongs.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r1.anchor: أي الذي لم يزل يحسن إليكم وأنتم تبارزونه بالعظائم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r2.claim: Repeating “before the torment comes” and retaining the preposition conveys God's gentleness toward those unable to defend themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r2.anchor: ولما كان من النفوس ما هو كالبهائم لا ينقاد إلا بالضرب , قال منبها أيضا علة رفقه بإثبات الجار

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r3.claim: The torment comes suddenly, which is especially difficult for people to bear.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r3.anchor: ولما كان الأخذ على غرة أصعب على النفوس قال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r4.claim: They will not perceive the torment as it arrives or beforehand because of heedlessness, making it horrifying and contrary to settled expectation.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r4.anchor: أي ليس عندكم شعور بإيتانه لا في حال إيتانه ولا قبله بوجه من الوجوه لفرط غفلتكم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r5.claim: Imagining the coming regrets beforehand would let people prepare and avoid their causes.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r5.anchor: لو تخيلها قبل هجومه لحسب حسابه فباعد أسبابه

DURR-FULL:v7p236/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p236/r4.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
DURR-FULL:v7p236/r4.claim: ʿAtaʾ b. Yasar says the three verses beginning with “My servants who have transgressed” were revealed in Medina concerning Wahshi and his companions.
DURR-FULL:v7p236/r4.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار قال: نزلت هذه الآيات الثلاث بالمدينة في وحشي وأصحابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p42/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p42/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p42/r3.claim: After opening the door of hope, the passage joins its counsel to repent with its ban on despair, using the conjunction and imperative to urge prompt action.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p42/r3.anchor: لما فتح لهم باب الرجاء أعقبه بالإرشاد إلى وسيلة المغفرة معطوفا بالواو وللدلالة على الجمع بين النهي عن القنوط من الرحمة وبين الإنابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p42/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p42/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p42/r8.claim: Each group has its share in the commands: polytheists must turn to monotheism and Islam, while believers who sin should repent and increase good works; Muslims already possess Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p42/r8.anchor: نصيب المشركين الإنابة إلى التوحيد واتباع دين الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r1.claim: ‘The best of what was sent down’ is the Quran; this directive is chiefly for polytheists, since Muslims already follow it, as the description of God’s servants shows.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r2.claim: Ahsan is a superlative meaning complete goodness, not a comparison between parts, since everything in the Quran is good; the construction resembles Joseph preferring prison to what his tempters invited him to.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r2.anchor: اسم تفضيل مستعمل في معنى كامل الحسن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r3.claim: The annexation of ‘best’ to ‘what was sent down’ is an adjective annexed to the noun it describes.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r4.claim: The punishment is the previously mentioned worldly and afterlife punishment, both arriving suddenly without warning; the sword’s punishment reached them at Badr, and the afterlife punishment will come at resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44/r4.anchor: والعذاب المذكور في هذه هو العذاب المذكور قبل بنوعيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r7.claim: The Qurʾān contains clear beliefs, saving commands and prohibitions, promises for obedience and good, boundaries for sins, and threats; the best course is to understand and act, obey, refrain, and show forbearance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: واتبعوا أحسن معناه: أن القرآن العزيز تضمن عقائد نيرة وأوامر ونواهي منجية وعدات على الطاعات والبر وحدودا على المعاصي ووعيدا على بعضها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r8.claim: Aḥsan does not mean that some Qurʾān is better than other Qurʾān; all of it is best in relation to human conduct and its consequences.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r8.anchor: فهذا المعنى هو المقصود ب أحسن، وليس المعنى أن بعض القرآن أحسن من بعض من حيث هو قرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r9.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r9.claim: Al-Suddī says the best course is what God commanded in His Book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r9.anchor: قال السدي: الأحسن هو ما أمر الله تعالى به في كتابه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r10.claim: Baghtatan means suddenly and without an appointment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537/r10.anchor: و: بغتة معناه: فجأة وعلى غير موعد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p191#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p191#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p191#2/r1.claim: The instruction to follow the best of what was revealed is explained by the phrase in al-A'raf 145 about taking its best parts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p191#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم ﴾ قد بيناه في قوله ﴿ يأخذوا بأحسنها ﴾ الأعراف 145

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r3.claim: Some say listeners follow God's speech and practice its best, especially Qur'anic pardon, forgiveness, and patience with harm; all Qur'an is good, while the best depends on the person acting.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r3.anchor: وهذا معنى ما قال بعضهم : يستمعون قول الله ، فيتبعون أحسنه ويعملون بأفضله ، وهو ما في القرآن من عفو وصفح

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r4.claim: Al-Ashari and some leading scholars deny that one part of Qur'an is intrinsically better than another, since all is God's speech and ranking could imply inferiority elsewhere.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r4.anchor: ذهب الإمام أبو الحسن الأشعري رحمه الله وبعض الأئمة الأعلام إلى المنع ؛ لأن الجميع كلام الله

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r5.speaker: المحققون
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r5.claim: The preferred view is that God's speech about Himself is better than speech about other subjects; al-Ikhlas exceeds al-Masad for its mention of God's unity and attributes, while al-Masad has only the merit of God's speech.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r5.anchor: وذهب آخرون من المحققين ، وهو الحق كلام الله في الله أفضل من كلامه في غيره ، فقل هو الله أحد أفضل من تبت يدا أبي لهب

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r6.claim: Reports assigning special virtue and abundant reward to particular chapters and verses are too numerous to count.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r6.anchor: والأخبار الواردة في فضائل القرآن وتخصيص بعض السور والآيات بالفضل وكثرة الثواب في تلاوتها لا تحصى.

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r7.speaker: الغزالي
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r7.claim: In Jawhar al-Quran, al-Ghazali asks how some passages can be nobler if all are God's speech, then cites Prophetic descriptions of Yasin, al-Fatiha, the Throne Verse, and al-Ikhlas.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r7.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي رحمه الله في "جوهر القرآن" : كيف يكون بعض الآيات والسور أشرف من بعض مع أن الكل كلام الله

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r8.claim: Those hesitant to rank verses can understand Prophetic phrases such as best surah as referring to reward: the eternal speech is equal in merit, with difference in reward rather than in God's speech itself.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r8.anchor: ومن توقف في تعديل الآيات أول قوله عليه السلام أفضل سورة وأعظم سورة أراد في الأجر والثواب

BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r1.claim: The best revealed thing can mean the Qur’an, as in 39:23, or the binding duties rather than dispensations.
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r1.anchor: أي : القرآن كقوله تعالى : {الله نزل أحسن الحديث} (الزمر : 23) ، أو العزائم دون الرخص

BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r2.speaker: البيضاوي ومن تبعه
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r2.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī and those following him take the best as what brings greater safety and salvation, such as repentance and steady obedience.
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r2.anchor: قال البيضاوي ومن تبعه : ولعله ما هو أنجى وأسلم ، كالإنابة والمواظبة على الطاعة

BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r3.claim: Ḥasan says to obey God and avoid disobedience: revelation identifies evil to shun, the best to prefer, and permissible matters one may do or leave.
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن : الزموا طاعته واجتنبوا معصيته ، فإن الذي أنزل عليكم من ثلاثة أوجه : ذكر القبيح لتجتنبوه ، وذكر الأحسن لتؤثروه

BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r4.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation reads this as pointing to the good revealed by God, namely what calls people to Him, as in 33:46.
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r4.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن ما أنزل الله منه ما يكون حسنا ، وهو ما يدعو به إلى الله

BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r5.claim: Here the coming punishment means affliction and chastisement.
BURSEVI:v8p96#2/r5.anchor: {من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب} ؛ أي : البلاء والعقوبة

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r1.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib defines suddenness as something arriving unexpectedly, from where one does not anticipate it.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r1.anchor: قال الراغب : البغتة مفاجأة الشيء من حيث لا يحتسب ، ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالعذاب

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r2.claim: The punishment that arrives unexpectedly may be death, since it opens the way to and is joined to afterlife punishment.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالعذاب الآتي بغتة هو الموت ؛ لأنه مفتاح العذاب الأخروي

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r3.claim: People are unaware through heedlessness and cannot sense punishment's arrival in time to make amends or prepare.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r3.anchor: وأنتم} لغفلتكم. {لا تشعرون} لا تدركون بالحواس مجيئه لتتداركوا وتتأهبوا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109#2/r1.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109#2/r1.claim: Umar relates that some Muslims who had reverted to unbelief under persecution thought God would accept neither expiation nor repentance, even from themselves; after the Prophet reached Medina, 39:53–55 was revealed concerning them. Umar sent it to Hisham ibn al-As, who understood it as applying to their despair, then traveled to Medina and joined the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p109#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمير، عن عمر، رضي الله عنه، في حديثه قال: وكنا نقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r1.claim: The best thing revealed from God is the Mighty Quran; people should follow it before punishment comes suddenly, without their knowing or sensing it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r1.anchor: وهو القرآن العظيم، {من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة وأنتم لا تشعرون}

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r18.claim: Baghta means suddenly, as in an event catching someone unawares.
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r18.anchor: والبغتة: الفجأة، بغته الأمر بغتا، وباغته مباغتة.

JISHUMI:v8p6079/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6079/r19.claim: Baghta is accusative as a circumstantial expression (ḥāl).

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r10.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r10.claim: Al-Suddi says to follow what God commanded in the Book.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r10.anchor: أحدها : هو ما أمرهم الله به في الكتاب , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r11.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says to do what they were commanded and avoid what they were forbidden.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r11.anchor: الثاني : أن يأخذوا ما أمر وينتهوا عما نهوا عنه , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r12.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r12.claim: Ibn Isa says it means following abrogating rather than abrogated revelation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r12.anchor: الثالث : هو الناسخ دون المنسوخ , حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r13.speaker: ابن زياد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r13.claim: Ibn Ziyad says it is obedience to God in lawful and unlawful matters.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r13.anchor: الرابع : هو طاعة الله تعالى في الحرام والحلال قاله ابن زياد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r14.speaker: زيد بن علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r14.claim: Zayd ibn Ali says it means fulfilling obligations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r14.anchor: الخامس : تأدية الفرائض , قاله زيد بن علي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r15.claim: A further possibility is choosing strict duties over dispensations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r15.anchor: ويحتمل سادسا : أنه الأخذ بالعزيمة دون الرخصة

MUQATIL:39:55-60/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r1.claim: Follow the Qur’an’s best, meaning its teachings on obedience in lawful and unlawful matters, before sudden punishment arrives while you are unaware.
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r1.anchor: من القرآن { من ربكم } يعنى ماذكر من الطاعة من الحلال والحرام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60/r1.claim: The command to follow the best revelation parallels the description of those who listen and follow its best in 39:18.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60/r1.anchor: مثل قوله الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60/r2.claim: The punishment may catch you suddenly while you are heedless, as though you fear nothing because of your extreme inattention.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60/r2.anchor: أى يفجؤكم وأنتم غافلون كأنكم لا تخشون شيئا لفرط غفلتكم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r7.claim: “The best of what was sent down” is the Qur’an, all of which is good; the command means to follow it before sudden punishment arrives.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r7.anchor: { أحسن ما أنزل } هو القرآن وكله حسن،

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets following the best as adhering to God’s obedience and avoiding disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r8.anchor: ما قال الحسن: التزموا طاعته، واجتنبوا معصيته.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r9.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r9.claim: Al-Suddī says the best is what God commanded in His Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r9.anchor: وقال السدي: الأحسن ما أمر الله به في كتابه.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the best to mean the decisive verses and says to leave knowledge of the ambiguous verses to their Knower.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r10.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: يعني المحكمات، وكلوا علم المتشابه إلى عالمه.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd also says the Qur’an is best because God sent the Torah, Gospel and Psalms before commanding people to follow this miraculous revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r11.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: يعني المحكمات، وكلوا علم المتشابه إلى عالمه. وقال: أنزل الله كتبا التوراة والإنجيل والزبور، ثم أنزل القرآن وأمر باتباعه فهو الأحسن وهو المعجز.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r12.claim: Another explanation is that the Qur’an is best because it abrogates and rules over the earlier books, which have all been abrogated.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r12.anchor: وقيل: هذا أحسن لأنه ناسخ قاض على جميع الكتب وجميع الكتب منسوخة.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r13.claim: Other explanations identify the best as pardon, what God taught the Prophet outside the Qur’an (with Qur’anic revelation the best), or reports of earlier peoples.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r13.anchor: وقيل: يعني العفو لأن الله تعالى خير نبيه عليه السلام بين العفو والقصاص.

RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r1.claim: One interpretation of “the best of what was sent down” is the Qur’an, supported by the description “best discourse.”

RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r2.claim: Al-Hasan takes it as obeying God and avoiding disobedience: revealed material includes what is bad to avoid, lesser things not to desire, and the best to follow.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r2.anchor: قال الحسن معناه ، والتزموا طاعة الله

RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r3.claim: A third interpretation identifies the best revelation as the abrogating ruling rather than the abrogated one, citing God’s promise of a better or equivalent replacement.

RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r4.claim: The sudden punishment warning threatens and frightens people by describing punishment that overtakes them while they are unaware.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r4.anchor: والمراد منه التهديد والتخويف والمعنى أنه يفجأ العذاب وأنتم غافلون عنه

STUDYQURAN:39:55/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:55/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:55/r1.claim: As at 39:18, following the most beautiful revelation does not rank one part above another; it means acting according to revelation through obedience and avoidance of disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:39:55/r1.anchor: what is most beautiful of what God has revealed is not understood to mean that one part is more beautiful than another

STUDYQURAN:39:55/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:55/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:55/r2.claim: Another formulation is to practice what God enjoins and avoid what He forbids; revelation achieves its purpose when its injunctions are put into practice.
STUDYQURAN:39:55/r2.anchor: it is only when the injunctions contained in revelation have been put into practice that their purpose is achieved

STUDYQURAN:39:55/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:55/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:55/r3.claim: Some understand the phrase to mean the Quran is the best or most beautiful of God's revealed books, as in 39:23.
STUDYQURAN:39:55/r3.anchor: Some understand this verse to mean that the Quran is the best or most beautiful of the books that God has sent down

TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r6.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār that the three verses were revealed in Medina concerning Waḥshī and his companions.
TAB-FULL:v20p224#2/r6.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار، قال: " نزلت هذه الآيات الثلاث بالمدينة في وحشي وأصحابه

TAB-FULL:v20p232/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says to obey God's commands in the revelation and avoid its prohibitions; this is what following its “best” means.
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r1.anchor: وإنما معناه: واتبعوا مما أنزل إليكم ربكم من الأمر والنهي

TAB-FULL:v20p232/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r2.claim: “Best” does not imply that some Qur'an is better than other Qur'an: all of it is good, and the phrase covers its commands, prohibitions, reports, parables, stories, arguments, promises, and warnings.
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r2.anchor: من الأمر والنهي والخبر والمثل والقصص والجدل والوعد والوعيد أحسنه، أن تأتمروا لأمره

TAB-FULL:v20p232/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r3.claim: Al-Suddi glosses following the best as doing what the Book commands.
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r3.anchor: عن السدي، {واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم} [الزمر: 55] يقول: «ما أمرتم به في الكتاب»

TAB-FULL:v20p232/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r4.claim: The warning urges people to act before God's punishment arrives suddenly and overtakes them while they are unaware.
TAB-FULL:v20p232/r4.anchor: يقول: «من قبل أن يأتيكم عذاب الله فجأة»

TABATABAI:39:53/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.claim: The passage calls people to Islam and following revelation, warns of regret for excess and worldly arrogance, and contrasts the pious’ salvation with unbelievers’ loss; its tone conveys mercy.
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.anchor: أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يدعوهم إلى الإسلام واتباع ما أنزل الله ويحذرهم عما يستعقبه إسرافهم

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.claim: These seven verses form one connected discourse: the ban on despair prepares for the following calls to repentance, submission, and righteous action, so the first verse is not an isolated promise.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.anchor: كلام واحد ذو سياق واحد متصل ينهى عن القنوط

TABATABAI:39:54-55/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r4.claim: The address to follow what was revealed in its best form applies to believers and unbelievers, since the Qur’an was revealed to both.
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r4.anchor: الخطاب عام للمؤمن والكافر كالخطابات السابقة والقرآن قد أنزل إلى الفريقين جميعا

TABATABAI:39:54-55/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r5.claim: One reported interpretation takes the best revealed material as legal rulings of the lawful and unlawful, excluding narratives.
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r5.anchor: قيل المراد به اتباع الأحكام من الحلال والحرام دون القصص

TABATABAI:39:54-55/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r6.claim: Another interpretation means obeying commands and prohibitions: doing obligatory and recommended acts, avoiding forbidden and disliked acts, but not requiring the permitted.
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r6.anchor: وقيل اتباع ما أمر به ونهي عنه كاتيان الواجب والمستحب واجتناب الحرام والمكروه دون المباح

TABATABAI:39:54-55/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r7.claim: A third reported view restricts following the best to firm obligations and prohibitions.
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r7.anchor: وقيل الاتباع في العزائم وهي الواجبات والمحرمات

TABATABAI:39:54-55/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r8.claim: A fourth view takes the best as the abrogating material rather than what has been abrogated.

TABATABAI:39:54-55/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r9.claim: A fifth view treats the revealed material as the heavenly scriptures generally and the best revelation as the Qur’an.
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r9.anchor: وقيل ما أنزل هو جنس الكتب السماوية وأحسنها القرآن فاتباع أحسن ما أنزل وهو اتباع القرآن

TABATABAI:39:54-55/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r10.claim: He rejects reducing the phrase to any one reported subset because the previous command to submit already encompasses their contents, making the restriction repetitive without cause.
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r10.anchor: يشمل مضمون كل من هذه الأقوال فحمل قوله

TABATABAI:39:54-55/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r11.claim: The best revelation means addresses showing how to fulfill servanthood through belief and action, such as remembrance, love, true piety, and sincere religion; following them revives life, faith, deeds, and divine guardianship.
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r11.anchor: الخطابات التي تشير إلى طريق استعمال حق العبودية في امتثال الخطابات الإلهية الاعتقادية والعملية وذلك كالخطابات الداعية إلى ذكر الله تعالى

TABATABAI:39:54-55/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r12.claim: The warning against sudden deprivation fits inward reform: people delay what they treat lightly, and this is closer to reforming the heart than merely performing outward bodily acts; compare 8:24.
TABATABAI:39:54-55/r12.anchor: وهذا المعنى أمس بإصلاح الباطن منه بإصلاح الظاهر

TABRISI:39:51-55/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:39:51-55/r20.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says follow the best by doing what is commanded and leaving what is prohibited.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r20.anchor: لمأمور به وترك المنهي عنه فقد اتبع الأحسن عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:39:51-55/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r21.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:51-55/r21.claim: One view limits ‘the best’ to obligatory and supererogatory obedience, excluding permissible matters.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r21.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال أحسن ما أنزل لأنه أراد بذلك الواجبات والنوافل التي هي الطاعات دون المباحات

TABRISI:39:51-55/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r22.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:39:51-55/r22.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says ‘the best’ means abrogating rather than abrogated verses.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r22.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالأحسن الناسخ دون المنسوخ عن الجبائي

TABRISI:39:51-55/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r23.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:39:51-55/r23.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā calls that wrong: an abrogated ruling may be good, though acting on the abrogating ruling is better.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r23.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى وهذا خطأ لأن المنسوخ يجوز أن يكون حسنا إلا أن العمل بالناسخ يكون أصلح وأحسن

TABRISI:39:51-55/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:51-55/r24.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:51-55/r24.claim: Punishment comes suddenly at an unexpected time they do not know.
TABRISI:39:51-55/r24.anchor: أي فجاة في وقت لا تتوقعونه

THALABI:v8p245/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p245/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v8p245/r4.claim: Thaʿlabi adopts al-Hasan's gloss: follow God's obedience and avoid disobedience; revelation mentions evil to shun, lesser things not to desire, and good to prefer.
THALABI:v8p245/r4.anchor: ما قال الحسن: التزموا طاعته واجتنبوا معصيته، فإن الذي أنزل على ثلاثة أوجه:

THALABI:v8p245/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p245/r5.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v8p245/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the best revealed thing as what God commanded in the Book.
THALABI:v8p245/r5.anchor: وكذلك قال السدي: الأحسن ما أمر الله به في الكتاب.

THALABI:v8p245/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p245/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v8p245/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the best revealed things are the decisive verses; knowledge of the ambiguous verses is left to their Knower.
THALABI:v8p245/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد (واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم) يعني المحكمات

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r4.claim: The best thing sent down is the Qur'an, as also stated in 39:23.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r4.anchor: أي: القرآن، كقوله: { الله نزل أحسن الحديث }

ELMALILI:39:53-55/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r11.claim: Before sudden punishment arrives unnoticed, one must sincerely submit to God and follow and apply the best of what He has revealed.
ELMALILI:39:53-55/r11.anchor: Haberiniz olmayarak ansızın başınıza azab gelmeden evvel hâlis müslüman olun

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r4.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r4.claim: Most exegetes take “punishment” here as worldly defeat of the polytheists by Muslims and “what was sent down” as the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r4.anchor: Müfessirlerin ağırlıklı görüşlerine göre bu âyetteki “azap”la dünyevî ceza, yani müşriklerin müslümanlar karşısındaki yenilgileri kastedilmiştir; “indirilen”den maksat ise Kur’an-ı Kerîm’dir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r5.claim: Translating this as “follow the best of what was revealed” could imply that some Qur’anic passages are better than others, so the authors reject that rendering.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r5.anchor: bu çeviri, Kur’an’ın bir bölümünün diğerinden daha güzel olduğu yönünde bir anlamaya yol açacağından isabetli görülmemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r6.claim: Following Ibn Ashur, the authors understand ahsan as “perfectly good,” encompassing all Qur’anic rulings, rather than as a comparative “better.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:54/r6.anchor: Bu durumda âyetteki ahsen kelimesini, “daha güzel olan” değil, Kur’an’ın bütün hükümlerini kapsamak üzere “kusursuz güzel olan” şeklinde anlamak gerekmektedir

ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r10.claim: The best thing sent down is the Quran, as shown by the earlier description of it as the best discourse.
ZAJJAJ:v4p357/r10.anchor: يعني القرآن ودليله: (الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.claim: The next section warns that polytheism and intercession will not save the idolaters but hasten ruin; success requires sincere turning to God and following His revealed Book, or their later regret will be useless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p564/r1.anchor: The path to success hinges on focussing attention towards God with sincerity of heart and on following this best of Books
